title: Hearing Buddy Bolden and comparing trumpeters
summary: He heard Bolden once around 1906-07, describes his power and how the fast life broke him, and compares him to Keppard.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: When did you hear Bolden? You say you heard him over here?

I heard him once, yes. I was a kid. I was just fixing to start out, you know, man. I was just fixing to go out and start playing. And he played over here once and I heard him play. Well, like I told you, he died a young man, you know. He wasn't old.
Do you remember about what year that was?
Well, that was around, I might say around 19, six or seven, around here, somewhere around there.
So you would have been almost?
Oh, I was around in my teens then, see.

Now, he was a fine-looking fellow and a healthy-looking fellow, but like, you know, the life, you understand what I mean? This fast life, it broke him all up. So many of them do the same thing, you know.
And you remember how he sounded and how he played?

Oh, yeah, he was powerful, you know. He had plenty of power, you know. He had a good style, you know, and bruised and all that stuff. But as far as anything else, there was nothing to it, you know. And just like all those other boys, I betty was a good man too. Chad Rene was another good man. They had good potentialities, but they never did develop them, you understand? They never did study, you see. They had the lip and everything. They made fine musicians up there to study, but they just went on playing, that's all, see. And made money, you understand? That's all they wanted, see. That's all it was, see.
What about Bolden? Does anybody who's made records or who's around today play anything like him?

Well, I don't know. It's practically, you take certain types now. You take Bolden and, say, Freddie Keppert, now he died in Chicago. They were mostly on the same style. They were powerful trumpet players and they mostly, well, the improvisation is always going to be a little different, you know, and they're no two men alike, you understand? But it's the similarity there, you understand what I mean, between them and the style was just a forceful trumpet player, you understand? Just strong and came out.
